title: Stack vs Queue: LIFO vs FIFO
excerpt: A stack is LIFO (last in, first out): push and pop at the same end. A queue is FIFO (first in, first out): add at the back, remove from the front.
author: BountyCode Team
body:
## Stack — LIFO

Push and pop at the same end (the top). Used for undo, browser back, function-call stack, expression evaluation.

## Queue — FIFO

Add at the back (enqueue), remove from the front (dequeue). Used for BFS, printer queues, task scheduling.

## In Python

Use a `list` as a stack (`append`/`pop`). Use `collections.deque` as a queue — `list.pop(0)` is O(n).

## Practice it

Build a stack and a queue, then solve the Stacks & Queues practice challenges.
code:
# Stack: LIFO
stack = []
stack.append(1); stack.append(2)
print(stack.pop())   # 2

# Queue: FIFO (use deque)
from collections import deque
q = deque()
q.append(1); q.append(2)
print(q.popleft())   # 1
